prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: switching after state check + Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner. Metocean Buoy. Duty Planner: Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Personnel: Marine Coordinator expected count; North/South Access Scanner; Personnel Tracking Console verified total; discrepancy→pause transfers. Post-incident: account personnel, reassess hazards, assign restart authority. Vessel recovery support: Rescue Coordinator sets objective, suspend authority, checks Load Sheet; Marine Coordinator assigns vessels, approach/departure plan; Duty Planner deconflicts; Weather Service forecasts area+route; Weather Analyst uncertainty; CTV only acceptable seas; Daughter Craft close-in if limits/comms adequate; SOV deck/lifting; HSE Officer reviews lifting/exclusion zones; Field Supervisor stops handling on zone entry; Electrical Technician isolates

Document units:
S657: Turbine Lockout remains in force until the responsible authority confirms that the equipment and work area are safe for subsequent activity.
S658: The Control Engineer provides technical guidance when recovery handling could affect turbine systems or restart readiness.
S659: If vessel capability, communications, or weather deteriorates, the Marine Coordinator pauses the recovery and agrees a safe holding position with the Vessel Master.
S660: After recovery, the Field Supervisor reports remaining hazards and confirms that temporary securing arrangements are adequate for transit.
S661: Visibility assessments are estimates of the conditions expected along a route and at a work site, rather than guarantees of clear sightlines.
S662: Reported visibility can vary across the wind farm as fog banks, rain, spray, and low cloud move through the area.
S663: Differences between observation times and locations can leave uncertainty even when individual reports are valid.
S664: The Weather Service forecast provides context for expected changes, but local conditions may develop sooner or differently than forecast.
S665: The Metocean Buoy provides a local reference that can help identify differences between forecast conditions and conditions at sea.
S666: A discrepancy between sources prompts review of the observation age, location, and surrounding weather conditions.
S667: The operational assessment records both the estimated visibility and the confidence that the estimate represents conditions at the intended work location.
S668: Low confidence is treated as an operational constraint even when the reported visibility appears adequate.
S669: The Duty Planner uses the Visibility Confidence Note when considering task readiness and the conditions that would require a decision to pause or defer work.
S670: The Maintenance Planning Engine can help identify tasks that may be rescheduled when visibility is uncertain.
S671: Task selection favors work that can be performed safely under the assessed conditions without relying on precise visual identification or close-range observation.
S672: Work requiring visual alignment, external inspection, or unobstructed observation is given a more conservative assessment.
S673: Use of the Blade Inspection Drone is deferred when uncertain visibility could prevent reliable control or interpretation of inspection imagery.
S674: The go or no-go decision considers the task method, crew competence, vessel capability, and the confidence in the visibility assessment.
S675: A favorable point estimate alone is not sufficient to authorize a task when the range of plausible conditions includes unsafe visibility.
S676: The Marine Coordinator reviews how uncertainty affects the planned transit, transfer location, and available alternatives.
